name: @odu/service
//cordis: THE ROW this package belongs to, read by the fence. A row is a capability the daemon serves — `ci` for the runs, `cache` for the buckets — and a package says which one it is behind so that nobody has to keep a second list.
//: THE CROSS-RUN AUTHORITY — see README.md. Everything the singleton web service OWNS: the registry projection every face reads the board from, the durable request receipts that make a lost reply reconcilable, and the handlers behind every one of @odu/service-client's procedures. What it deliberately does NOT own is a run: scheduling, log verdicts, retry closure and GitHub posting all stay in @odu/execution, which this package cannot import. It reaches them through PORTS (`./ports`) that the composition root binds.
//exports: A subpath pattern, for the reason @odu/execution's manifest gives: this package ships from this tree with its only consumers (`packages/cli` and the roots in `src/`), so a curated surface here would be a list nobody reads rather than a promise somebody depends on.
//dependencies: The wall runs service → service-client → run-history → run-client, and `@odu/execution` is ABSENT ON PURPOSE — src/closure.test.ts asserts it, because the day this package imports the coordinator is the day the service can no longer be reasoned about without one. `@odu/cordis` is the shared vocabulary: the `Principal` type a `Caller` carries, which the host resolves and every row reads. The @kolu/* sources are hydrated from a Nix pin (see bunfig.toml at the root) and so are absent here by design; the closure test pins the hydrated set instead.
